name: Liraglutide
route: Daily injection under the skin with a pen
status: FDA-approved: type 2 diabetes (2010) and weight management (2014); generic versions now available
mechanism: Mimics the gut hormone GLP-1 to release insulin when blood sugar is high, slow stomach emptying and reduce appetite
uses: Type 2 diabetes in adults and children 10 and older
Lowering heart risk in type 2 diabetes with heart disease

article.summary: Liraglutide (Victoza, Saxenda) is a once-daily GLP-1 injection, FDA-approved for type 2 diabetes and for weight management in adults and teens. Generic versions are available.
article.takeaway: Liraglutide was one of the first long-acting GLP-1 drugs and remains widely used, now also as lower-cost generics. At the 3 mg weight-loss dose, adults lost an average of **8.4 kg versus 2.8 kg** on placebo over a year.[^1] In people with type 2 diabetes and heart disease, it cut major cardiovascular events by **13%**.[^2] It needs a daily shot and produces less weight loss than newer weekly drugs such as semaglutide.[^3]
glance: Type 2 diabetes, cardiovascular risk reduction, chronic weight management
Injection under the skin once a day, at any time, with or without food
SCALE weight trials, the LEADER heart outcomes trial and pediatric trials

blocks.text: GLP-1 (glucagon-like peptide-1) is a hormone released by the intestine after eating. It prompts insulin release when glucose is high, curbs glucagon, slows stomach emptying and signals fullness to the brain. The body's own GLP-1 is cleared within minutes.

Liraglutide is 97% identical to human GLP-1, with a fatty-acid chain that lets it bind albumin in the blood and resist breakdown. That stretches its action to about a day, enough for one injection daily. Weekly drugs that came later, such as [semaglutide](/peptides/semaglutide), built on the same idea with a longer-lasting design.

rows: Type 2 diabetes in adults and children 10 and older; lowering cardiovascular risk in adults with type 2 diabetes and heart disease[^4]
Long-term weight management in adults with obesity or overweight plus a related condition, and in teens 12 and older with obesity who weigh more than 60 kg[^5]
Fixed combination with long-acting insulin for type 2 diabetes

blocks.text: Generic liraglutide matching both Victoza and Saxenda is sold by several manufacturers.

rows: Lost 8.4 kg vs 2.8 kg on placebo at 56 weeks; 63% lost at least 5% of body weight[^1]
9,340 adults with type 2 diabetes and high heart risk
Heart attack, stroke or cardiovascular death in 13.0% vs 14.9% on placebo[^2]
BMI fell at least 5% in 43% vs 19% on placebo[^6]
Weight fell 6.4% vs 15.8% with weekly semaglutide over 68 weeks[^3]

blocks.text: A 2025 trial in children aged 6-11 also found meaningful drops in BMI, but as of 2026 the US label for weight management starts at age 12.[^7][^5]

Both products start at 0.6 mg a day. For diabetes, adults move to 1.2 mg after a week and to 1.8 mg if needed.[^4] For weight management, the dose rises by weekly steps to the 3 mg target; teens can step up more slowly and may stay at 2.4 mg if 3 mg is not tolerated.[^5] Injections go under the skin of the belly, thigh or upper arm.

items: **Common:** nausea, diarrhea, constipation, vomiting and reduced appetite, mostly early on
**Serious but less common:** pancreatitis, gallbladder disease, kidney injury from dehydration and serious allergic reactions
**Boxed warning:** thyroid C-cell tumors in rodents; not for people with a personal or family history of medullary thyroid cancer or MEN 2
**Low blood sugar** when combined with insulin or sulfonylureas
**Before surgery:** slowed stomach emptying can raise aspiration risk under anesthesia

blocks.text: In the adolescent trial, BMI crept back up after treatment stopped, a pattern also seen in adults.[^6]

evidence.label: Strong: large randomized and outcome trials
evidence.text: Liraglutide has more than 15 years of use and large randomized trials behind it, including a cardiovascular outcomes trial with nearly 9,400 people.[^2] For weight loss it is less potent than newer weekly options.[^3]

faq.q: Are Victoza and Saxenda the same drug?
faq.a: Yes. Both are liraglutide. Victoza is dosed up to 1.8 mg for diabetes, and Saxenda goes up to 3 mg for weight management.

faq.q: Is liraglutide as effective as semaglutide?
faq.a: Not for weight loss. In the STEP 8 head-to-head trial, average weight loss was 6.4% with daily liraglutide versus 15.8% with weekly [semaglutide](/peptides/semaglutide).[^3]

faq.q: Is there a generic version of liraglutide?
faq.a: Yes. Generic liraglutide equivalent to Victoza and to Saxenda is available from several manufacturers, which can lower the cost.
